g.text: 4 · Does the procedure work when the truth is known?

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7280

g.text: 200 simulated meta-analyses per cell: 60 studies, shared controls, missing SDs, τ = between-study SD

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #6b7280

g.text: True mean lnRR 0.375 (moderator effect 0.15). MNAR: studies with larger true effects omit SDs more often. Complete-case analysis is unbiased under MCAR but

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #6b7280

g.text: loses precision, and under MNAR is biased (−0.05…−0.44) with CI coverage 0.03–0.60. CV̄ imputation keeps every study: bias ≤ 0.010, coverage 0.92–0.975 in all

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #6b7280

g.text: cells. Ignoring the shared-control covariance changes almost nothing; unweighted study means perform similarly because τ dominates the sampling variance. A

text.style: font-size: 5.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #6b7280

g.text: true moderator of 0.15 lowers new-study RMSE by only 1–4 %, as in the real data.
